title: WeilConjectures.zetaSeries_rational (Dwork rationality)
statement: Let k be a finite field and f:X->Spec k a morphism of schemes that is locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For a finite field k with q=#k elements, a scheme X and a morphism f:X->Spec k, the zeta series Z(X,t)=f.zetaSeries in Q[[t]] [sk-def-zeta] is Z(X,t)=exp(sum_{n>=1} N_n t^n/n), substituted into the formal exponential series, where N_n=f.pointCount n is the number of k-morphisms Spec F_{q^n} -> X (morphisms g with g followed by f equal to the map induced by k -> F_{q^n}), F_{q^n} being the model FiniteField.galoisExtension k n = the splitting field over k of X^{q^n}-X, and N_n=0 (junk value) if this set is infinite. A polynomial with integer coefficients is viewed in Q[[t]] through its coefficientwise image in Q[t] [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map, def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. Then there are polynomials P,Q in Z[t] [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with constant coefficient Q(0)=1 [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient] such that Z(X,t)*Q = P in Q[[t]] [def-weil-formal-power-series]. No smoothness, properness or separatedness is assumed.

proof.text: Write $k_0=k$, $q=\#k$, and $X_0=X$ with structure map $f$. The finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] applies because $f$ is locally of finite type and quasi-compact. The convention [sk-def-zeta] defines its degree-$n$ point-count field as the splitting field of $T^{q^n}-T$ over $k_0$, counts $k_0$-morphisms with value zero for an infinite set, and takes the formal exponential with the terms for $n\geq1$. These are exactly the fields, point counts and formal exponential in the target; the coefficient of degree zero in the exponent is zero. Thus its $Z(X_0,T)$ is the specified $f.zetaSeries$. No separatedness, smoothness or properness has been inferred.

source.place: Definition of point counts and zeta series, with the splitting-field model and infinite-cardinality convention.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-weil1] to this finite-type $k_0$-scheme. Its statement gives $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $B(0)=1$ and $B(T)Z(X_0,T)=A(T)$ in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$. The coefficientwise inclusion [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map] and polynomial inclusion [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series] mean precisely the maps $\mathbf Z[T]\to\mathbf Q[T]\to\mathbf Q[[T]]$ appearing in the comparator equation. Set $P=A$ and $Q=B$. Commutativity of the power-series ring changes $BZ=A$ into $ZQ=P$, so these witnesses satisfy both required clauses. The additional Euler-product conclusion of the cited theorem is not needed.
